title: A supplied finite-stage span eventually becomes pointed elementary etale
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $B$ and projections $p_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $r\in I$, a point $b\in B$, and suppose the canonical maps $\kappa(p_i(b))\to\kappa(b)$ are isomorphisms for every $i\ge r$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $V_r,P_r,Q_r$ be affine schemes of finite presentation over $S_r$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], equipped with arbitrary $S_r$-morphisms $\alpha_r:V_r\to P_r$ and $\beta_r:V_r\to Q_r$. For $i\ge r$ and $T_r\in\{V_r,P_r,Q_r\}$ write $T_i=T_r\times_{S_r}S_i$, $T_B=T_r\times_{S_r}B$, and $\pi_{T,i}:T_B\to T_i$ for the canonical projection; write $\alpha_i,\beta_i,\alpha_B,\beta_B$ for the actual pullback arrows [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $z\in V_B$ lies over $b$, both $\alpha_B,\beta_B$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and their induced maps $\kappa(\alpha_B(z))\to\kappa(z)$ and $\kappa(\beta_B(z))\to\kappa(z)$ are isomorphisms. Then there is $k\ge r$ such that for every $j\ge k$ the schemes $V_j,P_j,Q_j$ are affine of finite presentation over $S_j$, both arrows $\alpha_j,\beta_j$ are etale, and, putting $z_j=\pi_{V,j}(z)$, $x_j=\pi_{P,j}(\alpha_B(z))$, $y_j=\pi_{Q,j}(\beta_B(z))$, one has $\alpha_j(z_j)=x_j$, $\beta_j(z_j)=y_j$. The canonical maps $\kappa(z_j)\to\kappa(z)$, $\kappa(x_j)\to\kappa(\alpha_B(z))$, $\kappa(y_j)\to\kappa(\beta_B(z))$ are isomorphisms, as are $\kappa(x_j)\to\kappa(z_j)$ and $\kappa(y_j)\to\kappa(z_j)$ induced by $\alpha_j,\beta_j$.

proof.text: For each $T_r\in\{V_r,P_r,Q_r\}$, the affine fibre-product formula shows that $T_j$ is affine. Base-change permanence gives finite presentation of $T_j\to S_j$. Since a finite-presentation algebra is finitely generated (use its same polynomial generators), $P_r,Q_r$ are locally of finite type over $S_r$. Apply the map-over-base finite-presentation lemma to $V_r\to S_r$ and each of $P_r,Q_r\to S_r$: the supplied arrows $\alpha_r,\beta_r$ are locally of finite presentation. This does not assume these arrows are etale at stage $r$.

proof.text: The transition maps are affine by affine target-locality, using the one-member cover of each affine target and the affine source. Apply affine-chart etale descent to $\alpha_r$ with the whole affine schemes $S_r,P_r,V_r$ as $W,V,U$, respectively. Its limit hypothesis is precisely etaleness of $\alpha_B$; step 1 supplies local finite presentation. Thus $\alpha_j$ is etale for all $j\ge k_\alpha\ge r$. Apply it again to $\beta_r$ with whole charts $S_r,Q_r,V_r$. Choose a common upper bound $k$ of $k_\alpha,k_\beta$. All $j\ge k$ satisfy both conclusions.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, sentence applying Limits Tag 07RP, lemma-descend-etale; all-later-stage affine-chart form.

proof.text: Fix $j\ge k$ and $T_r\in\{V_r,P_r,Q_r\}$. Pullback associativity identifies $T_B=T_j\times_{S_j}B$, with first projection $\pi_{T,j}$: both descriptions represent pairs with equal composites to $S_r$, by the fibre-product universal property. For $t\in T_B$ over $b$, put $t_j=\pi_{T,j}(t)$ and $b_j=p_j(b)$. Set $K=\kappa(b_j)$, $L=\kappa(b)$, $E=\kappa(t_j)$, and let $\lambda:K\to L$ be the assumed canonical isomorphism. The tensor product $E\otimes_K L$ is canonically $E$: the map $a\otimes c\mapsto a\,\lambda^{-1}(c)$ has inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, since the balancing relation gives $a\otimes c=a\lambda^{-1}(c)\otimes1$. This is a field, so the kernel of its map to $\kappa(t)$ is zero. The fibre-product point residue-field lemma therefore says that this tensor-to-$\kappa(t)$ map is an isomorphism. Its restriction along $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ is exactly $\pi_{T,j}^{\sharp}:\kappa(t_j)\to\kappa(t)$, by that lemma's compatibility clause. Consequently this canonical residue map is an isomorphism. Apply this to $t=z,\alpha_B(z),\beta_B(z)$ for $T=V,P,Q$, respectively.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, residue-field chain; Schemes Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product, residue-field sentence and its canonical tensor map.

proof.text: The actual pullback arrows satisfy $\alpha_j\pi_{V,j}=\pi_{P,j}\alpha_B$ and $\beta_j\pi_{V,j}=\pi_{Q,j}\beta_B$ by the defining projection identities. Evaluating at $z$ gives the asserted point equalities. Write $c_V,c_P,c_Q$ for the three canonical residue isomorphisms from step 3, and $a_B,b_B$ for the two assumed limit residue isomorphisms. Composition of the local ring maps and passage to residue fields give $c_V\alpha_j^{\sharp}=a_Bc_P$ and $c_V\beta_j^{\sharp}=b_Bc_Q$. Hence $\alpha_j^{\sharp}=c_V^{-1}a_Bc_P$ and $\beta_j^{\sharp}=c_V^{-1}b_Bc_Q$ are isomorphisms, for every $j\ge k$.
